thread:
alex: Heads up - we saw an odd routing behavior this morning during the canary. Canary v3 was set to 1% weight but after a header-based client test went out, v3 jumped to ~15% for a short window. Is header matching supposed to override weights or vice versa?
jamie: Headers normally have higher precedence in the current evaluator, but only for exact route matches. If there's a fallback weight route that matches the path, behavior can look like a jump if the header rule is broader.
alex: Example: we have a header rule `X-Alpha-Test: v3` -> route:v3 and a weighted default for /generate -> {v3:1%, v2:99%}. The client test had sticky cookies so some requests hit v3 even without the header after the first hit.
sasha: Sticky session + header affinity is the tricky bit. Our sticky cookie uses session buckets that can persist after header expires. We probably didn't clear the session on the test client.
megan: Hmm - UX question: should the Console show combined expected traffic when both header and sticky exist? Right now it shows the weight only, which is misleading.
jamie: I agree we need a console change. We should surface a "effective traffic" calc that simulates header and sticky overlap. Could be opt-in since exact numbers depend on client behavior.
console-bot: [analytics] Snapshot for route `/api/v1/generate` at 2026-02-27T08:12Z: weight-config={v3:1,v2:99}, header-overrides=2 active rules, sticky-enabled=true.
alex: For the routing engine, can we make evaluation deterministic: 1) explicit header match if present, 2) session affinity if no header, 3) weighted fallback. That order would stop weight from absorbing header traffic.
sasha: That ordering makes sense but we have to be careful about rule scoping. If header rule has path prefix /api/ then it matches multiple routes. Prefer more-specific path then header then weight?
jamie: Proposed precedence algorithm: - exact path + header > exact path + weight > prefix + header > prefix + weight > global weight. Also prefer explicit route.order if provided.
megan: Sounds good. For Console wiring: show a tooltip on the traffic graph explaining precedence and show a "what-if" switch to include header overrides.
deploy-bot: Triggering canary policy update: PR #4217 merged by jamie. Rolling out evaluator change to staging.
alex: quick note: add a guard in evaluator so header rules with `allow_sticky: false` will not persist sessions. We need a per-rule flag.
sasha: On telemetry, add tags: {"rule.match_type": "header|sticky|weight", "cohort": "canary-v3"} so we can split traces by why a request chose a variant.
jamie: Yep will add those tags. Also add a short-lived metric `route.effective_share` that reports observed percent per variant after precedence.
megan: Follow-up UX item: when you create a header override in Console, prompt "Will this take precedence over existing weight/affinity?" with toggles for apply-to-existing-sessions.
alex: OK action list: jamie implements precedence change + telemetry tags, sasha does session flag and evaluator tests, megan wires Console messaging and the what-if sim. I'll own integration test and a short runbook for on-call if yields spike.
megan: I'll add a UI mock to the design doc and link PRs.
jamie: Plan to deploy to staging in ~30m, monitor `route.effective_share` and `5xx` rate.
deploy-bot: Staging deploy started for canary-eval-update at 1766000300.
alex: Thanks everyone. Filing follow-up ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-8792 (notes + runbook).
megan: :thumbsup:
